findings.description: The check changed from `fg is not None` to truthiness `if fg:`. A color value of 0 (integer 256-color index for black) is falsy, so it is silently skipped.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `style(text, fg=0)` or `bg=0`. The color is dropped and no escape code is emitted, so the user gets uncolored text instead of black. Previously 0 was valid and emitted `38;5;0`.

findings.description: `_interpret_color` no longer validates ints, tuples or lists. Out-of-range or malformed values are accepted and produce invalid ANSI codes; bool is treated as int.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `fg=300`, `fg=(1,2)`, `fg=(300,0,0)`, or `fg=True`. A 2-tuple raises ValueError on unpacking, which is an unhelpful error. Out-of-range values and True silently emit invalid escape sequences such as `38;5;300` or `38;5;1`.

findings.description: Unknown colors now raise TypeError instead of ValueError, and only KeyError is caught. An unhashable value such as a dict raises an uncaught TypeError from the lookup `_ansi_colors[color]`.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `style('x', fg='nocolor')`. Callers that catch ValueError for an unknown color no longer catch it, which changes the exception contract.
